name: Henry Kissinger
role: US National Security Advisor (1969-1975) and Secretary of State (1973-1977)
summary: Kissinger was a realist who organised US foreign policy around the balance of power and great-power diplomacy: detente and arms limits with the Soviet Union, the opening to China, and negotiation to end the Vietnam War. His record includes the bombing of Cambodia, support for the Chilean and Argentine juntas and covert action in Chile and Angola, which critics say ignored human rights and civilian harm. He treated legitimacy as acceptance by the major powers rather than justice, and his later statements on Ukraine moved from opposing NATO membership (2014) to supporting it (2023).

reduce-immigration.rationale: In late 2023 he called admitting so many people of different culture and religion to Germany a grave mistake; this is a remark on immigration levels, not a general policy statement.

nation-first.rationale: Pursued US national interest through realpolitik, prioritising balance-of-power arrangements over multilateral cooperation, including the opening to China and the Soviet arms talks.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Contested: he ordered military and covert force for strategic aims, but argued against acting on human rights grounds, as in his 1976 meetings with Pinochet and his handling of warnings about East Pakistan.

political-violence-never.rationale: Record: in 1970 he backed a push for a military coup to stop Allende's inauguration, and later supported the Chilean and Argentine juntas; he gave no general statement on political violence.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred: he defined legitimacy in order as acceptance by the major powers and not as justice, and set public opinion and morality aside; he stressed that civilisations hold different concepts of order.

force-without-un.rationale: His record includes the bombing of Cambodia and covert operations in Chile and Angola, none of them approved by the UN Security Council.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Record: he cancelled a US warning to Chile against political assassinations and is reported to have worked to thwart Carter-era efforts to indict Chilean agents over the Letelier killing.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Contested: he called NATO a decaying alliance in 1973, but in 2023 he backed tying Ukraine to NATO, which implies support for alliance commitments.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: in 2023 he backed NATO membership for Ukraine and said neutrality was no longer meaningful, which presumes NATO's collective defence; Article 5 itself was not discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Contested: in 2016 he advised accepting Crimea as Russian, and in May 2022 he urged Ukraine to cede territory to restore the pre-invasion lines; he did not discuss the general legal status of annexation.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: As Secretary of State he pursued a compromise with Senate leaders over covert aid to UNITA and the FNLA fighting the MPLA government in Angola in 1975; Congress then cut off that aid.

defeat-communism.rationale: Contested: he pursued detente and coexistence with the Soviet Union and opened to China, while also backing anti-communist covert action in Chile in 1970.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Contested: he approved the bombing of Cambodia and backed operations in Vietnam, while calling the Vietnam war useless in 1972.

arms-reduction.rationale: Negotiated SALT I and the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty with Brezhnev, a record of arms limitation.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Record: he conducted secret channels, including the 1971 Beijing trip and secret Vietnam talks, so his practice ran against open diplomacy.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: his 1957 book argued that deterrence depends on usable nuclear forces, including small weapons held in reserve; it did not address unilateral disarmament directly.

national-resource-control.rationale: In 1974 he accepted Peru's sovereign right to nationalise property for public purposes, with compensation; this recognises national control over resources, not a general position.

notes: Changes of view: on Ukraine he said in 2014 that Ukraine should not join NATO and should be a bridge between East and West (s1); in December 2016 he advised accepting Crimea as Russian; in May 2022 he urged a return to the pre-invasion lines (s2); in January 2023 he called NATO membership for Ukraine an appropriate outcome (s7). The most recent clear position (2023) is used for NATO and Ukraine statements, and the 2022 territorial advice is recorded as low-confidence because a July 2022 interview points the other way (reported in Wikipedia). Contested: Chile 1970-73, Cambodia, Argentina 1976, Angola 1975. Not read in full: Diplomacy (1994), World Order (2014), On China (2011), White House Years, Years of Upheaval, and NSSM 200 (1974, population): archive.org full texts returned 401/404 to the downloader, and their positions were not answered except where cited above. Null answers on population, Holocaust, Israel-Palestinian and US domestic economics reflect the sources reachable in this session, not a verdict.
